lines.text: A narrow strip of coast and mountain, where Phoenician sailors spread the alphabet and many faiths learned to share one small country. This is Lebanon.
Nearly five thousand years ago, Tyre was founded on the coast. It grew famous for its purple dye, until Alexander took it after a long siege.
Tyre, Sidon and Byblos were the cities of Phoenicia. Their sailors founded Carthage, and their alphabet became the ancestor of Greek and Latin letters.
Many centuries and empires later, under Ottoman rule, local emirs governed the mountains as the Emirate of Mount Lebanon.
Kahlil Gibran, born in the mountains in 1883, would emigrate to America and write The Prophet, read around the world.
After the Ottoman Empire fell, France created the State of Greater Lebanon in 1920, with Beirut as its capital.
Fairuz was born in 1935. Her songs would make her the voice of Lebanon for generations.
In 1943 Lebanon's leaders made an unwritten National Pact, sharing power between its Christian and Muslim communities.
That same year Lebanon became independent from France, a small country with many faiths and a long memory.
Rafic Hariri, born in 1944, would make a fortune abroad and return as prime minister to rebuild Beirut.
Joseph Aoun, born in 1964, would rise to lead the army, and in 2025 to become president.
In 1975 the balance broke. For fifteen years civil war tore the country apart, and Beirut was split in two.
In 1982, after Israel invaded, Hezbollah was formed, a Shia party with its own armed force.
In 1989 the Taif Agreement shared power anew among the religious groups, and the war at last came to an end.
In 2005 Hariri was killed by a huge bomb. Vast protests, the Cedar Revolution, followed, and Syria's troops left.
A year later, war broke out between Israel and Hezbollah, and much of the south was left in ruins.
From 2019 the economy collapsed. Banks froze savings, the currency lost most of its value, and many fell into poverty.
Then in August 2020, a store of chemicals left for years at the port exploded, wrecking much of Beirut.
In 2024 Israel bombed and invaded Lebanon again, killing Hezbollah's leader, before a ceasefire in November.
From the ports of Phoenicia to the ruins of Beirut, Lebanon keeps rising again.
